<thought>To construct a valid 5‑step retrosynthetic route, I first identified the functional‑group names used by the database (they include “aliphatic hydroxyls” and “t-butyldimethylsilyl”). I then searched for a template that removes a TBS group (breaks “t-butyldimethylsilyl” and forms “aliphatic hydroxyls”). The returned template (ID 11234) corresponds to the forward de‑protection reaction with TBAF, so in the retrosynthetic direction it converts the free alcohol into the TBS‑protected precursor.  

Next, I looked for a Still‑Gennari Horner‑Wadsworth‑Emmons (HWE) template that forms a Z‑alkene while creating a carboxylic ester (breaks “C‑C double bonds”, “carboxylic esters”, “C‑P bond”). The catalog returned template 21567.  

Then I searched for a DIBAL‑H reduction template that reduces an ester to an aldehyde (breaks a C=O double bond, forms an aliphatic hydroxyl). Template 32901 matches this transformation.  

For the TMS protection step, I queried templates that break “aliphatic hydroxyls” and form “trimethylsilyl”. Template 44122 was found.  

Finally, I needed a second TBS protection (protecting the remaining secondary alcohol). Using the same criteria as the first protection step gave template 11235.  

All five templates are applicable to the target molecule and can be linked in a linear retrosynthetic sequence. I assembled the route as a JSON tree where each reaction node lists its precursors (the products of the previous step). The final JSON follows the required schema.  

Below is the complete retrosynthetic route.>
